comment.description: An optional note recorded with the decision — for example the reason for a denial. Surfaced to the requester.

AccessDecisionVerdict.description: An approver's verdict on a pending access request, as it appears on the wire: `0 = deny`, `1 = approve`.

durationSeconds.description:
How far the lease's end is pushed out, in seconds. Must be positive and no longer than the governing rule's
maximum extension duration.

reason.description: The justification recorded with the extension. Required to be non-empty.

AccessLeaseExtensionRequestModel.description:
A request to extend an active lease, identified by the route's lease id. The lease's end is pushed out by
Bit.Services.Pam.Api.Models.Request.AccessLeaseExtensionRequestModel.DurationSeconds; a justifying Bit.Services.Pam.Api.Models.Request.AccessLeaseExtensionRequestModel.Reason is required. Extensions are always auto-approved,
subject to the governing rule allowing extensions and the per-lease maximum not being reached.

requestId.description: The request this lease was born from.

cipherId.description: The cipher the lease grants access to.

collectionId.description: The collection the cipher belongs to.

ruleId.description: The access rule that gated the cipher at grant time. Not tracked in v1.

organizationId.description: The organization that owns the cipher.

requesterId.description: The user the lease was granted to (the original requester).

notBefore.description: When the lease's access window opens (UTC).

notAfter.description: When the lease's access window closes (UTC).

revokedAt.description: When the lease was revoked early (UTC); null unless it was revoked before expiry.

revokedByUserId.description: The user who revoked the lease; null unless it was revoked early.

revocationReason.description: The reason captured on early revocation. Recorded on the audit decision, not surfaced here in v1.

AccessLeaseResponseModel.description:
An access lease as its requester sees it: the originating request, its lifecycle Bit.Services.Pam.Api.Models.Response.AccessLeaseResponseModel.Status, and
revocation fields. Powers the request-submission envelope, the caller-scoped "my active leases" surface, and the
cipher access-state snapshot. Fields without a backing store in v1 (Bit.Services.Pam.Api.Models.Response.AccessLeaseResponseModel.RuleId,
Bit.Services.Pam.Api.Models.Response.AccessLeaseResponseModel.RevocationReason) are null.

reason.description: An optional note explaining the revocation. Recorded on the audit trail; not surfaced on the lease itself.

AccessLeaseRevokeRequestModel.description: A request to revoke an active lease early. Bit.Services.Pam.Api.Models.Request.AccessLeaseRevokeRequestModel.Reason is optional and retained for the audit trail.

AccessLeaseStatus.description:
The lifecycle state of an access lease, as it appears on the wire: `0 = active`, `1 = expired`,
`2 = revoked`.

id.description: The human approver's user id, or null for an automatic decision.

name.description: The human approver's display name; null for an automatic decision, or when the user could not be resolved.

email.description: The human approver's email; null for an automatic decision, or when the user could not be resolved.

comment.description: The optional note the approver left with the decision.

AccessRequestDecisionResponseModel.description:
One decision on an access request: who decided (Bit.Services.Pam.Api.Models.Response.AccessRequestDecisionResponseModel.DeciderKind), their identity for a human decision,
the verdict, an optional comment, and when. An element of Bit.Services.Pam.Api.Models.Response.AccessRequestDetailsResponseModel.Decisions
— the request's full decision log, oldest first.
            
For an automatic (access-rule) decision Bit.Services.Pam.Api.Models.Response.AccessRequestDecisionResponseModel.Id/Bit.Services.Pam.Api.Models.Response.AccessRequestDecisionResponseModel.Name/Bit.Services.Pam.Api.Models.Response.AccessRequestDecisionResponseModel.Email are null; for a
human decision they carry the approver (name/email denormalized by the server, null only when the user could not be
resolved).

cipherId.description: The cipher access was requested for.

collectionId.description: The collection the cipher belongs to, through which the request is governed.

organizationId.description: The organization that owns the cipher.

requesterId.description: The member who opened the request.

ruleId.description:
The access rule that gated the cipher and that this request is evaluated against, resolved once at submit
(oldest wins) and pinned on the request. Null for requests created before pinning existed.

leaseNotBefore.description:
The activation window resolved at submit — the bounds on WHEN this request may be promoted to a lease. Both
request modes collapse into it (on-demand → `now`..`now + duration`, scheduled → the chosen
start/end), so there is no separate duration or mode field; the length is Bit.Services.Pam.Api.Models.Response.AccessRequestDetailsResponseModel.LeaseNotAfter minus
Bit.Services.Pam.Api.Models.Response.AccessRequestDetailsResponseModel.LeaseNotBefore. In v1 the approved and leased windows are identical to this one.

leaseNotAfter.description: The end of the resolved activation window (UTC); see Bit.Services.Pam.Api.Models.Response.AccessRequestDetailsResponseModel.LeaseNotBefore.

reason.description: The optional justification the requester supplied when opening the request.

resolvedAt.description: When the request was approved, denied, or cancelled (UTC); null while pending.

expiredAt.description: Distinct from Bit.Services.Pam.Api.Models.Response.AccessRequestDetailsResponseModel.ResolvedAt; set when an approved request lapses unactivated. Not tracked in v1.

decisions.description:
The request's decision log, oldest first — one element per decision (human or automatic). Each carries who
decided (`deciderKind`), the verdict, and (for a human decision) the approver's identity and comment.
Empty only while pending. An array so multi-party approval lands without breaking the contract.

producedLeaseId.description: Set once an approved request has produced a lease.

extensionOfLeaseId.description: The parent lease if this is an extension request.

requesterName.description: The requester's display name, denormalized by the server; null only when the user could not be resolved.

requesterEmail.description: The requester's email, denormalized by the server; null only when the user could not be resolved.

AccessRequestStatus.description:
The lifecycle state of an access request, as it appears on the wire: `0 = pending`, `1 = approved`,
`2 = activated`, `3 = denied`, `4 = canceled`, `5 = expired`.

name.description: The rule's display name, shown wherever rules are listed and managed. Required; up to 256 characters.

description.description: Optional free-text describing the rule's intent. Has no effect on evaluation; surfaced to admins only.

enabled.description:
When false, the rule is inactive and does not gate access for the collections it governs. Defaults to
true so a request that omits the field creates an active rule.

singleActiveLease.description: When true, the rule enforces a per-cipher singleton (at most one active lease per cipher across all users).

defaultLeaseDurationSeconds.description:
Default lease duration in seconds, used to pre-fill a request opened under this rule. Null means the
backend default applies.

maxLeaseDurationSeconds.description:
Hard ceiling on the duration of any single lease granted under this rule, in seconds. Null means no
per-rule cap.

allowsExtensions.description:
When true, a member holding an active lease under this rule may extend it once (always auto-approved), by up
to Bit.Services.Pam.Api.Models.Request.AccessRuleRequestModel.MaxExtensionDurationSeconds.

maxExtensionDurationSeconds.description:
The longest a single extension may run, in seconds. Required to be positive when
Bit.Services.Pam.Api.Models.Request.AccessRuleRequestModel.AllowsExtensions is true.

collections.description:
The complete set of collections this rule governs. The rule's associations are replaced to match
exactly this set; an empty array clears all associations.

organizationId.description: The organization this rule belongs to.

name.description: The rule's display name, shown wherever rules are listed and managed.

description.description: Optional free-text describing the rule's intent. Has no effect on evaluation; surfaced to admins only.

enabled.description: When false, the rule is inactive and does not gate access for the collections it governs.

conditions.description:
The condition tree that decides how access is granted under this rule — for example requiring human
approval, or restricting to certain times of day or source IPs. Returned as a JSON object; null when the
rule imposes no conditions.

singleActiveLease.description: When true, the rule enforces a per-cipher singleton (at most one active lease per cipher across all users).

defaultLeaseDurationSeconds.description:
Default lease duration in seconds, used to pre-fill a request opened under this rule. Null means the
backend default applies.

maxLeaseDurationSeconds.description:
Hard ceiling on the duration of any single lease granted under this rule, in seconds. Null means no
per-rule cap.

allowsExtensions.description:
When true, a member holding an active lease under this rule may extend it once (always auto-approved), by up
to Bit.Services.Pam.Api.Models.Response.AccessRuleResponseModel.MaxExtensionDurationSeconds.

maxExtensionDurationSeconds.description: The longest a single extension may run, in seconds. Set when Bit.Services.Pam.Api.Models.Response.AccessRuleResponseModel.AllowsExtensions is true.

collections.description: The complete set of collections this rule governs.

revisionDate.description: When the rule was last modified (UTC).

lastKnownRevisionDate.description: The last known revision date of the Cipher that this attachment belongs to.

AuthType.description: Specifies the authentication method required to access a Send.

active.description:
Whether the discount is a recurring/perpetual discount with no expiration date.

This property is true only when the discount has no end date, meaning it applies
indefinitely to all future renewals. This is a product decision for Milestone 2
to only display perpetual discounts in the UI.
Note: This does NOT indicate whether the discount is "currently active" in the billing sense.
A discount with a future end date is functionally active and will be applied by Stripe,
but this property will be false because it has an expiration date.

percentOff.description:
Percentage discount applied to the subscription (e.g., 20.0 for 20% off).
Null if this is an amount-based discount.

amountOff.description:
Fixed amount discount in USD (e.g., 14.00 for $14 off).
Converted from Stripe's cent-based values (1400 cents → $14.00).
Null if this is a percentage-based discount.
Note: Stripe stores amounts in the smallest currency unit. This value is always in USD.

end.description: The instant the discount stops applying (Stripe Discount.end). Null = no end date / perpetual.

durationInMonths.description: For a repeating coupon, the number of months it applies. Null for once/forever.

appliesTo.description:
List of Stripe product IDs that this discount applies to (e.g., ["prod_premium", "prod_families"]).

Null: discount applies to all products with no restrictions (AppliesTo not specified in Stripe).
Empty list: discount restricted to zero products (edge case - AppliesTo.Products = [] in Stripe).
Non-empty list: discount applies only to the specified product IDs.

BillingCustomerDiscount.description: Customer discount information from Stripe billing.

limitCollectionCreation.description:
If set to true, only owners, admins, and some custom users can create and delete collections.
If set to false, any organization member can create a collection, and any member can delete a collection that
they have Can Manage permissions for.

limitCollectionDeletion.description:
If set to true, only owners, admins, and some custom users can delete collections.
If set to false, any member can delete a collection that they have Can Manage permissions for.

allowAdminAccessToAllCollectionItems.description:
If set to true, admins, owners, and some custom users can read/write all collections and items in the Admin Console.
If set to false, users generally need collection-level permissions to read/write a collection or its items.

limitItemDeletion.description:
If set to true, members can only delete items when they have a Can Manage permission over the collection.
If set to false, members can delete items when they have a Can Manage OR Can Edit permission over the collection.

useRiskInsights.description:
If true, the organization can use the Risk Insights feature. This is a reporting feature that provides
insights into the security of an organization.

useOrganizationDomains.description: If true, the organization can claim domains, which unlocks additional enterprise features.

useAdminSponsoredFamilies.description: If set to true, admins can initiate organization-issued sponsorships.

syncSeats.description: If set to true, organization needs their seat count synced with their subscription.

useAutomaticUserConfirmation.description:
If set to true, the organization can use the automatic user confirmation feature.
This automatically confirms users in the Accepted state without requiring manual admin intervention.
There are significant security risks to this and access is manually controlled by our internal teams.

useDisableSmAdsForUsers.description: If set to true, disables Secrets Manager ads for users in the organization

usePhishingBlocker.description: If set to true, the organization can use the phishing blocker feature.

useMyItems.description:

policy is enabled.

useInviteLinks.description: If set to true, the organization can generate reusable sharable invite links to invite users to the organization.

usePam.description: If true, the organization is subscribed to the Privileged Access Management (PAM) product.

lifecycle operations such as subscription cancellation and disabling for non-payment.

An organization is an entity that allows users to share vault items and
manage billing, access control, and other enterprise features depending on the plan.
